cards.text: Jesus is still talking to His disciples, and now He tells them, 'Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.' Apron on, lights on, and NOBODY is hitting snooze.

cards.question: Jesus says His disciples should be like servants who are waiting up for someone. Who are those servants waiting for?

answers.text: A guest from a far country

cards.question: The master is coming back from a wedding banquet. When he comes and knocks, the servants who are ready can open the door for him at ___.

cards.text: The master walks up, the lamps are lit, the servants are on watch, and Jesus calls those servants blessed. Then comes a twist I had to read TWICE.

cards.question: The master gets home and finds his servants on watch. What does he do for them?

answers.text: He waits on them at the table
He gives each one a bag of silver
He lets them sleep until morning

cards.text: The MASTER dresses himself to serve, has the servants recline at the table, and waits on THEM. That's like your boss walking in and saying, sit down, I'll take your shift, and friend, I would faint, gold base and all.

cards.question: The master might come late, in the second or third watch of the night. Even then, the servants he finds alert are still blessed.

cards.text: Then Jesus switches pictures. Now it's a homeowner, and a thief who's coming to break in, and let me tell you, friend, no thief in history has ever sent a calendar invite that says 'Break-in, 2 AM, please confirm.'

cards.question: Jesus says that even if the homeowner had known the hour the thief was coming, he still couldn't have stopped the break-in.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings it all home with the Son of Man, a name Jesus uses for Himself (Luke 9:22). Sit up straight for this one, friend, because I am, and I don't even HAVE a back.

cards.question: Jesus says, 'You also must be ___, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not ___.'

cards.text: Peter, one of Jesus's disciples (Luke 6:13-14), has a question about the parable. Every meeting needs one person brave enough to unmute, and today that's Peter.

cards.question: What does Peter want to know about the parable Jesus just told?

answers.text: Whether it's for them or everyone
When the master will come back
Which servant the master will reward

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question of His own: who then is the faithful and wise manager the master puts in charge of his servants? Friend, if somebody asked me that, I'd be pointing my whole mustache at myself going ME, it's ME, pick ME.

cards.question: The master puts that manager in charge of his servants. What's the manager's job?

answers.text: Give them their portion on time
Keep count of the master's flocks

cards.question: When the master returns and finds that manager doing his job, he puts him in charge of all his possessions.

cards.text: But suppose that same servant says in his heart that his master won't be back for a long time. Uh oh.

cards.question: The manager decides his master won't be back for a long time. What does he start doing?

answers.text: Beating the servants and getting drunk

cards.question: The master of that servant comes back on a day and at an hour the servant expects.

cards.text: And the master cuts that servant to pieces. That's a hard line, friend, and there's no joke that belongs on it.

cards.question: The master assigns that servant a place with the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus compares two servants who both do things worthy of punishment: one knows his master's will and doesn't get ready, and the other doesn't know. One read the memo, one never got the memo, and friend, I have been BOTH of those guys.

cards.question: The servant who knew his master's will gets fewer blows than the servant who didn't know.
Jesus says that from everyone who has been given much, ___ will be required.

cards.text: And from the one entrusted with much, even more will be demanded, so a guy handed a whole planet of ovens takes that line VERY personally. Stick around, friend, because Jesus isn't done teaching yet.

findings.problem: The card uses the burning lamps from Luke 12:35 as well as the master's return and the servants being found on watch in Luke 12:37, but it cites only Luke 12:37. The citation is narrower than the verses the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Cards 4 and 5 refer to "that manager," and cards 8 and 10 refer to "that servant," relying on earlier cards instead of identifying the person within the question. Cards 8 and 10 are especially unclear because they do not say that this is the servant who decided his master was delayed and began beating the other servants.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the master cuts the servant to pieces. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out "unbelievers" rather than "strangers" or "beggars," so the blank asks for wording the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
